Article Title: Watch: CCTV captures moment Delhi's Satya Niketan building collapsed, leaving 6 dead
Article Text:
The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road

10 patients taken to Trauma Centre

MCD orders demolition of dangerous building

NEW DELHI: CCTV footage has captured the moment a multi-storey building collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan area, killing six people and triggering a major rescue operation.The building, which housed a boys' paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus, collapsed around 1.30 pm on Sunday while repair and construction work was underway. The death toll rose to six after one more person rescued during the night was declared dead.The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped.Multiple agencies, including the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Service, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Delhi Disaster Management Authority, have been involved in the operation."One more person was rescued during the night but was brought dead, taking the toll to six," Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel said, PTI reported.Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has also been ordered. Officials are continuing efforts to trace people allegedly connected with the incident.To the residents, the collapse felt like a quake. “We felt the ground shake.When we ran outside, we saw that a house had completely collapsed,” said Roshan Pal, a student from Lucknow.“When I came out, a cloud of dust was spreading in all directions. That’s when we realised that the building had collapsed. We started removing one part of a wall soon after. Seven students were under it,” said Rahul Gaur, a resident, TOI reported.According to AIIMS, the JPN Apex Trauma Centre received 10 patients injured in the building collapse. Of the 10 patients, five were brought dead, while another patient who was in critical condition later succumbed to injuries.Three patients have been admitted and are undergoing treatment. One of them underwent limb surgery, while another patient with minor injuries was discharged after observation.Investigators are examining whether construction work carried out in the basement may have contributed to the collapse.Initial inquiries suggested that the basement was prone to waterlogging, which may have weakened the structure. Investigators are now examining whether construction work aggravated the situation and contributed to the collapse.The MCD is also looking into the matter. Similar concerns over basement work, water accumulation and the structural condition of the building have emerged in the preliminary probe.Police are likely to examine whether permission had been obtained for the work and why construction was being carried out during the monsoon, sources said. "The building owner, contractor and labourers will be interrogated," an investigator said, TOI reported.It was not immediately clear whether the building owner had obtained permission for the construction or whether the work was being carried out illegally, allegedly in connivance with local authorities.According to the MCD, the premises of Building/House No. 13, Satya Niketan, New Delhi, was found to be in a "ruinous, dangerous condition" and posed a threat to people occupying, visiting or passing by the building as well as those in the neighbourhood.Under Section 348 of the DMC Act, 1957, read with Section 491 of the Act, the MCD has ordered the property to be demolished within three days of receipt of the order.The order said that if the owner fails to comply within the specified period, the MCD will demolish the building and recover the demolition charges as arrears of tax.The collapse has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated areas of Delhi.Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations.“What is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?” Selja said.Former Delhi chief secretary Omesh Saigal said the incident should not be viewed in isolation and raised concerns over unauthorised construction in parts of the capital."Look at the kind of buildings constructed in Delhi—I would say that in some areas, one in five buildings is unauthorised; either the blueprints weren't approved, extra floors were added, or the construction is substandard," he said.Saigal also called for restrictions on new construction in areas that are already overcrowded. "At the very least, we should ban new construction in these areas. We must halt new construction or stop sanctioning building plans, for areas that are already over-congested and over-built. These are the things that need to be addressed," he added.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped. Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has been ordered.

NEW DELHI: The death toll in the Satya Niketan building collapse in Delhi rose to six as search and rescue operations continued at the site, with teams clearing heavy debris and looking for any remaining trapped persons. Hours after the building collapse in a student-dominated area near Delhi University’s South Campus, the MCD has ordered action against illegal buildings with four or more storeys.One more body was recovered during late-night operations, taking the total number of fatalities to six.Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Fire Service, Delhi Police and other agencies continued rescue operations at the site as they worked to remove the debris.The collapse that took place on Sunday afternoon, has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest (PG) accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated parts of the national capital.The Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the incident and directed that an FIR be registered against the building owner, the chief minister’s office (CMO) said.The decision was taken following an on-site review and a preliminary assessment of the incident, the CMO said.“Following an on-site review and based on the preliminary assessment, the chief minister has ordered a Magisterial Inquiry of the incident and an FIR against the building owner,” the CMO said.It added that those found responsible for the incident would be held fully accountable and face the strictest provisions of the law.Meanwhile, Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations. She said students are sent to Delhi with hopes of building their future and questioned who would be held responsible for their safety.“What is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?” Selja said.Former Delhi chief secretary Omesh Saigal said the incident should not be viewed as an isolated case, claiming that similar incidents occur every few months. He also raised concerns over unauthorised construction in parts of Delhi.Saigal alleged that some buildings either have unapproved blueprints, additional floors added later or substandard construction, and questioned whether authorities responsible for approving building plans had adequately checked their safety."Look at the kind of buildings constructed in Delhi - I would say that in some areas, one in five buildings is unauthorised; either the blueprints weren't approved, extra floors were added, or the construction is substandard," he said.He also called for restrictions on new construction in areas that are already overcrowded and over-built, saying authorities should consider stopping the sanctioning of new building plans in such areas and examine the safety of existing structures."At the very least, we should ban new construction in these areas. We must halt new construction—or stop sanctioning building plans—for areas that are already over-congested and over-built. These are the things that need to be addressed," he added.NSUI President Vinod Jakhar described the situation as extremely grave and said rescue operations were continuing under difficult conditions."Rescue operations are ongoing, and conditions are dire. Almost all the students being pulled out are dead. We tried our best to get those students out; we actually succeeded in rescuing about three of them. Had the medical facilities, medical teams, police, and fire brigade arrived on time—had all necessary resources and responsible officials been present promptly—perhaps more students could have been saved. But the BJP has no disaster management plan. Just look at how the country's Home Minister inaugurates a grand BJP office in Goa today, while here, a building collapses. BJP offices never collapse because they are built using money extorted from PG and coaching centre operators. Our only demand is justice for the students. Several of our colleagues have also sustained serious injuries. There is absolutely no accountability," Jakhar told news agency ANI.Meanwhile, Delhi Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha president Rajat Choudhary said the situation remained serious and appealed for speedy rescue efforts. He said ambulances and doctors were present in large numbers and urged both the Delhi and Central governments to ensure that those trapped were rescued quickly.Choudhary also appealed to political parties to avoid politicising the tragedy and instead extend support to the affected families and those involved in the rescue operation."This is not the time for politics; those affected were someone's children. Instead of playing politics, one should offer support. The opposition should not do this; they should stand in solidarity," he said.In a separate response, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) ordered the immediate sealing of all illegal constructions with more than four floors and warned of strict action against officials found responsible.“All illegal constructions with more than four floors will be immediately sealed, and strict action will be taken against the guilty officials, leading to their immediate dismissal. These orders will be implemented with immediate effect,” the MCD said.
Article Summary: Death toll in Satya Niketan building collapse in Delhi rises to six. MCD orders action against illegal buildings with four or more storeys. Delhi government orders magisterial inquiry into the incident and an FIR against the building owner. Congress leader questions the safety of students living in such accommodations.

Article Title: 'Cracked skull' wasn't all: In eye of storm, 'influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj
Article Text:
Swatantra Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district.

A provocative online presence

The hunt for Bhardwaj

(With inputs from PTI)

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the government doing enough to hold influencers accountable for their actions online? Yes, they are taking action No, they need to do more 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Long before the viral video in which he boasted about assaulting a Jantar Mantar protester’s father, 'influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj had built a sizeable following through provocative posts, political associations and incendiary remarks.Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district on Friday, hours after Delhi Police assured protesters from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) that he would be arrested within 72 hours.Bhardwaj is accused of assaulting the father of student activist Nishu Azad during a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on July 20.His detention came after a clip from an interview went viral in which Bhardwaj is heard claiming that he had "cracked the skull" of the father."Do you know which section this crime attracts? Section 307. He needed 60 stitches. The man was being taken away in an ambulance in serious condition. His daughter was standing outside the police station and saying that she would die by suicide if her father didn't get justice."But I was not even jailed. The world should know this. I was out and about through the night," Bhardwaj is heard saying in the video.He then named several political leaders while explaining why, according to him, he had little reason to fear arrest."I have the blessings of Hanuman upon me. And secondly, Kapil Mishra is my elder brother. They say Kapil Mishra called and I was released. Chirag Paswan is my elder brother. How many leaders do you know? Do you know Modi ji? Modi ji is also my elder brother. I have everyone's support," he claimed.There is, however, no evidence to establish that any of the political leaders named by Bhardwaj intervened on his behalf in the case.The viral clip also brought renewed attention to Bhardwaj's older social media posts and videos.According to news agency PTI, his Facebook page, which has around 327,000 followers, contains posts focused on cow protection, attacks on Muslims and critics of the government, as well as photographs appearing to show his proximity to political figures and official events.Some older videos circulating on social media purportedly show him making inflammatory remarks about Muslims and government critics. In others, he boasts about his political connections and claims he does not fear arrest.His online presence suggests that the persona seen in the viral clip was not an isolated episode, but part of a broader public image he had cultivated over time.On Thursday, a day before his detention, Bhardwaj shared a screenshot showing his name among the trends on X, captioning it, "Love you all Virodhi".He also posted a photograph on Instagram showing a 'kada' on his wrist with the caption "Feel the power!". The post appeared to reference a Delhi Police statement that Kumar had been injured by a 'kada' and "not by any weapon".His social media accounts also featured photographs with political leaders, including Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Delhi minister Kapil Mishra and Union minister Chirag Paswan.Paswan said on Friday that Bhardwaj had misused his name and the names of other leaders.The Union minister for food processing industries said he had lodged a complaint against Bhardwaj and demanded action against him."No action despite the accused admitting to an attack that could have been fatal sets a bad example; I take responsibility for ensuring justice for the family," Paswan said.Bhardwaj's accounts also included what appeared to be AI-generated images of him with women wearing burqas or hijabs.One particularly violent image, posted on 22 May, showed Bhardwaj holding the bloodied chin of a man. The accompanying text referred to "Mughal" and included the words "aa gaya swad".His Instagram account, which had around 184,000 followers, was deactivated on Friday. He also has a verified account on X with more than 6,400 followers.The viral video intensified demands for action against Bhardwaj, with protesters raising the issue during the CJP demonstration in Delhi on Friday.Police subsequently deployed several teams to trace him.According to police officials, Bhardwaj had travelled to Bulandshahr and was staying in Naithla village. He allegedly fled the village on a motorcycle towards Khurja before a police team could apprehend him.He was wearing a helmet, apparently in an attempt to conceal his identity, police said.Local residents told TOI that Bhardwaj had arrived in Bulandshahr early on Friday, allegedly to evade arrest, and had taken shelter at the home of a local family.While there, he interacted with some journalists and reportedly repeated his claims about the alleged assault during the CJP protest.Bhardwaj was staying at the house of Harishankar Sharma, a Naithla resident who works as a cab driver in the Delhi-NCR region.Sharma said he had met Bhardwaj during an earlier journey.“Bhardwaj called me and said he wanted to come to my house to meet me. He arrived early in the morning along with another man. Initially, I did not suspect anything. But when media persons started arriving at my village, I sensed something was wrong,” Sharma said.Sharma said Bhardwaj later asked to borrow his motorcycle, saying he would return “within five minutes”.“Then I came to know that Delhi Police had detained him. It was only after that I learnt that he was wanted in a criminal case in the national capital. I still do not know much about the case,” Sharma said.The detention came after CJP representatives said Delhi Police had assured them that Bhardwaj “will be arrested within 72 hours”.The case has since drawn attention not only to the alleged assault but also to the online persona Bhardwaj had built through provocative posts, political associations and claims of influence.
Article Summary: Swatantra Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district on Friday. He is accused of assaulting the father of student activist Nishu Azad during a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on July 20. His detention came after a clip from an interview went viral in which he claimed he had "cracked the skull" of the father.

NEW DELHI: Faced with turmoil over the state leadership in Punjab, Congress has heaved a sigh of relief as politicians cutting across factional lines have welcomed Sachin Pilot 's appointment as party incharge of the poll-bound state in place of Bhupesh Baghel.Former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Channi and Lok Sabha MP Sukhjinder Randhawa, who lead the dissident group gunning for state president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, extended their best wishes to Pilot. Warring too has welcomed Pilot's appointment.While Channi expressed his "heartfelt thanks" to the Congress brass for "this important decision", Randhawa wished Pilot the "very best for this important responsibility" and said his experience, leadership and connect with the people will give new strength and momentum to the Congress organisation in the state.The duo's first reaction has assured the leadership that the decision on Pilot is in the right direction, though many believe coming days will decide if they are ready to move on from their demand for Warring's ejection. Sources said there is very little likelihood of a change in the state leadership now.Two months ago, Congress was shocked by the outbreak of dissidence in Punjab that goes to polls in February and where the ruling AAP has already launched its campaign for re-election.Congress had announced its election-related committees on July 1, but they have proved a non-starter as the appointments were followed by open groupism that brought the party activities to a halt.Now, Congress is hoping for a new start. The party is planning a statewide yatra in Punjab that will feature Rahul Gandhi, and it may be held towards the end of Sept or early Oct. The schedule will have to take care of the festivals falling in between.Congress hopes removal of Baghel, who had become another target for the dissidents as he strongly opposed their demand to replace Warring, would settle the flux, and allow the party to kickstart its outreach to people.
Article Summary: Congress has heaved a sigh of relief as politicians cut across factional lines have welcomed Sachin Pilot's appointment as party incharge of the poll-bound state. Sources said there is very little likelihood of a change in the state leadership now.

Article Title: India, 163 others vote at UNGA for map with bigger Africa, shrunk North America
Article Text:

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the adoption of the new Equal Earth map by the United Nations General Assembly? Yes No Unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

United Nations General Assembly voted Friday to adopt a new world map that makes the African continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe, drawing ire from Washington.Aimed at "a more accurate representation" of continental landmasses, the resolution was supported by 164 countries, including India. US voted against it and six nations abstained.The new map, known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection, improves "the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world", the resolution said. It urges member states to use the new map in place of the traditional Mercator projection.Foreign minister Robert Dussey of Togo, which sponsored the resolution, said maps "guide education, nourish imagination, and influence collective perceptions"."They are therefore never neutral; when they present a distorted image of our planet, they risk perpetuating inaccurate representation that is passed down through generations," he said.African Union Commission chair Mahmoud Ali Youssouf said, "Beyond cartography, this initiative underscores the importance of representing Africa on the basis of objective and scientifically established realities...Africa must be represented as it truly is: in its true dimensions and in its rightful place in the world."US, however, slammed the resolution, saying such moves are "the reason this institution is losing its credibility". Representative Yaryna Ferencevych said, "Instead of focusing on genuine problems... this body is debating map projects from the 16th century and their role in promoting reparations and cognitive justice."The Mercator projection was designed for maritime navigation by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569. It focused on depictions of the shapes and angles of land masses but their relative sizes were often inaccurate, largely due to the challenge of rendering a three-dimensional globe onto a two-dimensional map.It inflated northern regions and compressed equatorial ones, making Europe and North America appear much larger, while shrinking Africa and South America. Africa appears to be roughly as big as Greenland, though at 30.3 million sq km, it's about 14 times as large.France, which co-sponsored the resolution, announced Friday it would abandon the Mercator projection, in which "US, Russia and China take on a disproportionate visual prominence". Foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot said, "Changing maps obviously doesn't change the world," "But correcting a distorted representation is already an act of truth."
Article Summary: The United Nations General Assembly voted Friday to adopt a new world map that makes the African continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe. The resolution was supported by 164 countries, including India. US voted against it and six nations abstained. The new map, known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection, improves "the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world"

NEW DELHI: Six people were killed and five were rescued after a five-storey boys' paying guest (PG) accommodation collapsed in southwest Delhi's Satya Niketan area on Sunday, officials said. Rescue operations were under way to search for any remaining people trapped under the rubble.The collapse involved a building known as 'Hostel Daze', which was being used as a boys' PG. An adjacent building also collapsed, according to eyewitnesses.JPN Apex Trauma Centre (AIIMS), on late Sunday, informed that it received 10 patients from the Satya Niketan building collapse. Four were brought dead, while one critically injured patient later succumbed. Three are admitted and undergoing treatment, one underwent limb surgery, and one with minor injuries was discharged after observation.The AIIMS Trauma Centre said eight injured people were brought to hospitals following the incident. Seven were taken to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, while one was admitted to Safdarjung Hospital. Two of those brought to AIIMS were declared brought dead.The death toll later rose to three, with authorities confirming that six people had been rescued from the rubble.Two National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams were deployed at the site, while two additional teams were kept on standby, NDRF Inspector General NS Bundela said. Rescue teams were working in coordination with the State Disaster Response Force, Delhi Fire Service and other agencies.The Delhi Fire Service received information about the collapse at around 1.30 pm, following which eight fire tenders and multiple rescue teams were rushed to the spot. Police also cordoned off the area as rescuers searched through the debris.Eyewitnesses said several students were believed to be inside the building when it collapsed. A local resident claimed the PG had around 15 rooms, with two to three students staying in each room, and that around 35 to 40 students were residing on its upper floors.Residents said many students were inside their rooms because it was Sunday. Several locals joined the rescue operation, removing debris with their hands and whatever tools were available.Residents alleged that construction or repair work was under way in the basement and that water had accumulated there. A local resident who has lived in the area for around two decades claimed the building's foundation was weak.Another resident said he had been inside the building shortly before the collapse and managed to get out minutes before the structure came down.The adjacent building was also reportedly leaning after the collapse, raising concerns about the safety of nearby structures.Residents said most students staying at the PG were from Kerala, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh and attended colleges including Motilal Nehru College, Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College and Sri Venkateswara College.One resident said students were paying around Rs 12,000 per bed at the accommodation. Residents also raised concerns about the condition of buildings in the congested locality, where several residential properties have reportedly been converted into student PG accommodations.Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta visited the site and reviewed the ongoing search and rescue operation. Emergency teams continued clearing the rubble and searching for anyone who may still be trapped."No one will be spared," she says.The Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the incident and directed that an FIR be registered against the building owner, the chief minister’s office (CMO) said.The decision was taken following an on-site review and a preliminary assessment of the incident, the CMO said.“Following an on-site review and based on the preliminary assessment, the chief minister has ordered a Magisterial Inquiry of the incident and an FIR against the building owner,” the CMO said.It added that those found responsible for the incident would be held fully accountable and face the strictest provisions of the law.Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences over the deaths in the Satya Niketan building collapse and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured. He said authorities were working at the site and assisting people affected by the incident.
Article Summary: Death toll rises to six after boys' PG building collapses in southwest Delhi. Rescue operations under way to search for any remaining people trapped under the rubble. Rescue teams working in coordination with State Disaster Response Force, Delhi Fire Service and other agencies. Residents alleged that construction or repair work was under way in the basement.

Behera's Gita and ISKCON links

NEW DELHI: IIT Mandi has set up an inquiry after a Bhagavad Gita-themed poster displayed on its campus during Janmashtami celebrations described Shudras as being meant to "serve higher classes", triggering controversy over caste discrimination.Institute Director Laxmidhar Behera said the poster was part of a student-led event and had not been approved by the institute. He said he was "shocked" when he learnt about the display and stressed that IIT Mandi does not support caste-based discrimination.In an email to the IIT Mandi community on Sunday, Behera described the development as an "Outright condemnation of recent poster display within campus". He said the poster, displayed on September 4, had not been endorsed by the institute "in any manner"."I have personally fought against caste-based discrimination in any form in every forum. I have instituted an enquiry committee in this matter such that the institute campus is never used for any such violation of social harmony. I fully empathise with members of our community who have been hurt by this incident," he wrote.Behera said IIT Mandi was committed to "the values of equality, social justice, scientific temper" and the principles laid down in the Constitution."The institute strongly condemns any form of caste based discrimination," he said, urging members of the campus community to "stand together against such biases/discrimination in any form".Speaking to PTI, Behera said the poster had been prepared for a student event. He said the inquiry committee included faculty members and representatives from different social categories, including members of the Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes.The poster, titled "Bhagavad Gita - The Timeless Wisdom", was put up outside the institute's auditorium during Janmashtami celebrations.It divided society into four groups mentioned in the Bhagavad Gita, namely Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. It described Brahmanas as those who "spread God's message", Kshatriyas as those who "protect society and spirituality" and Vaishyas as those who "drive economy, support others".For Shudras, however, the poster listed their role as "serve higher classes", which became the focus of the controversy.The poster also quoted a Bhagavad Gita verse stating that the four divisions of human society were created according to the "three modes of material nature and the work associated with them".Behera said he had been away from IIT Mandi and returned on Saturday. He said he learnt about the controversy on Sunday morning."I have not seen the poster. I don't want to take a side here and let the panel decide," he told PTI.The controversy has also drawn attention to Behera's long association with the Bhagavad Gita and ISKCON.According to his official IIT Mandi profile, Behera has spent 27 years teaching what he describes as the "universal principles of peace through Bhagavad Gita". He is also known as "HG Lila Purushottam Das" and is the founder of the proposed Bhaktivedanta University, whose website describes it as an ISKCON initiative.Behera currently teaches a three-credit course on the Bhagavad Gita at IIT Mandi.He defended ISKCON's position on caste, saying the organisation opposes discrimination and promotes equality."ISKCON is the only organisation that strictly and strongly speaks against caste-based discrimination. In ISKCON, pujaris are also from the Shudra community. Muslims are also pujaris," he claimed."We are against casteism in all forms. All occupational duties are according to guna and karma," he added.Behera also highlighted what he said was increased representation of marginalised communities at IIT Mandi during his tenure. According to him, the institute had no OBC, SC or ST faculty members when he joined, while their numbers have since risen substantially. The IIT director has previously faced criticism over his public views.In 2023, he asked students to take a pledge against eating meat and linked landslides and cloudbursts in Himachal Pradesh to cruelty towards animals. In 2022, shortly after becoming IIT Mandi director, a video surfaced in which he claimed to have helped a friend's family get rid of "evil spirits" through chanting holy mantras.More recently, IIT Mandi's Indian Knowledge System and Mental Health Applications Centre held a conference in June that included sessions on the Bhagavad Gita, Ayurveda and reincarnation. Behera was among its general chairs and co-organised a session titled "Reincarnation, OBEs and afterlife communication".The institute's inquiry committee will now examine how the poster was prepared, displayed and presented during the student-led event.
Article Summary: IIT Mandi sets up inquiry after Bhagavad Gita-themed poster sparks controversy. Poster described Shudras as being meant to "serve higher classes" Institute Director Laxmidhar Behera said the poster was part of a student-led event. He said he was "shocked" when he learnt about the display and stressed that IITMandi does not support caste-based discrimination.

NEW DEHI: A 21-year-old woman allegedly jumped into the Chenab River in Doda district on Saturday after speaking to her father over the phone and telling him, "This is my life," before saying, "Bye-bye, papa. " A joint rescue operation was launched soon after the incident, but there was no immediate trace of her.The incident took place around 2 pm at the Shiva Dal bridge near Prem Nagar. Police, personnel from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and local volunteers joined the search operation in the river after the woman, identified as Payal Devi, reportedly jumped from the bridge.A video purportedly recorded by passersby who attempted to discourage her from taking the step shows Devi saying "bye-bye" before jumping into the Chenab. The video subsequently went viral on social media.Officials said the circumstances that led to Devi taking the extreme step were not immediately known.The final conversation between Devi and her father, Krishan Lal, came shortly before she disappeared into the river.According to Lal, Devi had gone to a mela earlier in the day. She later called him and said that she was feeling unwell and intended to consult a doctor.When the doctor was reportedly unavailable, Devi began making her way back. At some point, she apparently got onto a motorcycle.Lal said he subsequently received a call from a person who was accompanying his daughter. The person told him that Devi had run towards the river.The development prompted Lal to speak to his daughter over the phone. He said he repeatedly asked her what had happened and whether somebody had said or done anything to her.Lal recalled Devi telling him, "Nobody should come near me."He continued trying to understand what had happened and urged her to explain why she was behaving that way.According to Lal, Devi responded, "No, papa. This is my own life. My heart tells me that I should go this way."She then told her father, "Bye-bye, papa," before the call ended, he said.The moments before Devi jumped were also reportedly captured on video.The video, which was said to have been recorded by passersby at the bridge, shows people attempting to discourage her. Despite their efforts, she reportedly jumped into the Chenab.The footage later circulated widely on social media, drawing attention to the incident and the efforts of those present to prevent her from taking the step.Following the incident, police, SDRF personnel and local volunteers launched a joint rescue operation in the Chenab River.Teams searched the river for Devi, but officials said there was no trace of her.The search operation was undertaken after the reported jump from the Shiva Dal bridge, a location near Prem Nagar in Doda district.As the rescue teams continued their efforts, the reasons behind Devi's actions remained unclear. Article Summary: Payal Devi, 21, reportedly jumped into the Chenab River in Doda district on Saturday. NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Sunday backed students protesting against alleged irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations, saying that "every student is tormented by the BJP regime".In a post on X, Rahul said thousands of students were protesting in Maharashtra because their trust in the system had been "shattered"."In Maharashtra, thousands of students are on the streets, protesting peacefully - the reason isn't just one exam or recruitment, but a trust that's been shattered by the entire system," Rahul said."Whether it's the central or state government, every student is tormented by the BJP regime. Article Title: With bare hands, lone warrior cleans up dumpyard of a river
Article Text:
21-year-old BSc student has been a solitary warrior against civic mess and pollution in his hometown

BHOPAL: His online followers know him as 'Bittu Tabahi'. In reality, Surendra Singh Choudhary is the exact opposite of what the moniker 'Tabahi', meaning destruction, implies.For the past seven months, this 21-year-old BSc student has been a solitary warrior against civic mess and pollution in his hometown, Biaora in MP's Rajgarh district, picking up plastic bottles, tangled weeds and other solid waste from Ajnar river, which had virtually become a dumpyard.With no heavy machinery or protective gear at his disposal, he removed the garbage with his bare hands, often at great risk to his health.Bittu's dogged pursuit has helped restore a section of the river, earning him widespread praise across the country and an invite from CM Mohan Yadav Saturday. They had a warm exchange at the CM's residence in Bhopal, where Yadav assured Bittu of every possible support from govt.The chief minister also shared a video on X, calling Bittu a "son of Biaora" who not only restored Ajnala (the river stretch passing through Biaora) to its original form through sheer resolve and effort, but also sent out a larger message that one man's determination is all it takes to bring meaningful change.There were also reports that the CEO of an organisation from the Netherlands had offered him a job, but Bittu said he had only heard this from media reports. "I am yet to receive any information about it first hand," he told TOI.Encouraged by his success, Bittu, whose parents work in the health department, has decided to expand his work. "My sole objective is to keep my hometown clean. I have decided to take my work to other public places," he said.Bittu started his mission on Republic Day this year. Upset that everyone complained about the mess, but none - including the municipal administration - addressed it, the college-goer decided to get his hands dirty. From removing garbage piles on streets to pulling out weeds from water bodies, his activism eventually drew national attention.Unfortunately, his selfless service is being undone by the same people he is trying to help. In his interaction with the chief minister, Bittu shared the pain of watching people throw garbage into the river again, oblivious to the effort that went into cleaning it. "I don't know why people keep dumping waste into the river," he said, his voice betraying anger.The silver lining is that the local municipal corporation has now woken up to its civic mandate, and has deployed JCBs and Poclain machines to clear waste piles from the streets. However, the larger problem - habitual littering and a lack of collective ownership - remains unaddressed.
Article Summary: Surendra Singh Choudhary, 21, has been a solitary warrior against civic mess and pollution in his hometown, Biaora. With no heavy machinery or protective gear at his disposal, he removed the garbage with his bare hands. Bittu's dogged pursuit has helped restore a section of the river, earning him widespread praise across the country.

CJP’s student campaign

Meeting ahead of UP polls





LUCKNOW: CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka met Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, according to news agency PTI.Accroding to SP chief spokesperson Rajendra Chaudhary said, Ashutosh Ranka and SP chief Akhilesh Yadav met in the Lucknow on Thursday evening. After police used a lathi charge during the CJP’s agitation at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, party MP Dimple Yadav and Azamgarh MP Dharmendra Yadav visited the protest site and expressed solidarity with the students.Akhilesh Yadav has also spoken in support of the student movement led by the CJP on several occasions.The meeting comes at a significant time, with Uttar Pradesh scheduled to hold Assembly elections early next year.The SP has been targeting the BJP-led state government over issues such as unemployment, education and inflation.Yadav, a former Uttar Pradesh chief minister, has repeatedly raised concerns over school closures. Article Title: Blinkit's Mangaluru storage sealed after customer finds worm inside egg
Article Text:
Food safety officials inspected a Blinkit facility in Mangaluru after a consumer found a worm in an egg





MANGALURU: Food safety officials in Karnataka inspected a Blinkit online retail facility in Mangaluru after a consumer alleged that a worm was found inside an egg purchased through the quick-commerce platform.The complaint was reportedly submitted to Health Minister U T Khader, following which officials inspected the facility operating from Falnir Square in the city's Falnir area.During the inspection, officials found packets containing broken eggs and directed the facility staff to immediately remove and dispose of the affected stock, according to an official release.As a precautionary measure, the storage room was temporarily closed and sealed to allow thorough cleaning and sanitisation of the food storage area.The Food Safety Department said it would issue a notice to the establishment seeking an explanation over the incident. Further action will be decided based on the inspection findings and the response submitted by the facility management.The inspection comes amid increased scrutiny of food safety and hygiene standards in Karnataka. In a separate action, the Department of Food Safety and Drug Administration recently closed and seized a kitchen at Chairman's Club in Sahakaranagar's Dollars Colony area of Bengaluru after officials found multiple alleged violations during a special inspection drive conducted on September 3.Officials said around 40 kg of expired chilli was found and seized during the inspection. The department also flagged improper labelling of certain food products, unhygienic conditions in food preparation and storage areas, alleged use or storage of unauthorised artificial colours, lapses in food handling and storage practices, and the storage of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food products together.The department said it would continue inspections and take legal action against food businesses found violating food safety and hygiene norms.
Article Summary: Food safety officials in Karnataka inspected a Blinkit facility in Mangaluru. A consumer alleged that a worm was found inside an egg purchased through the quick-commerce platform. The complaint was reportedly submitted to Health Minister U T Khader. During the inspection, officials found packets containing broken eggs.

A celebration turned tragedy in Mexico killed at least 10 people while leaving 64 injured after pyrotechnic material exploded during a religious festival in Temascalcingo on Saturday night. The explosion collapsed walls and sent hundreds of people fleeing in panic, authorities said.The blast occurred beside the Nuestra Señora de la Luz church in the central Mexican town where residents were gathered to watch a fireworks display being held as part of celebrations for the local patron saint. The municipality is located about 160 kilometres (100 miles) northwest of Mexico City.The explosion brought down the walls of surrounding buildings and triggered a fire in the town square.Footage circulating online from the accident shows people dancing around with the firework structure in celebration. It was after a couple of rounds that the pyrotechnics began going berserk. Due to the nature of the structure, the smoke from the firework billowed rapidly in the air before the people could react to the mishap.Videos from the aftermath were also circulated online showing people moving through thick smoke and scattered debris as they searched for survivors.Some victims were reportedly trapped beneath collapsed structures.The cause of the explosion has not yet been established. The Mexico State Attorney General’s Office has opened an investigation into the incident.A local bishop said two priests were among those injured in the blast.The explosion occurred during a traditional festival ritual in which a straw bull fitted with fireworks is burned and carried around the town. Video footage showed the blast striking as crowds stood outside the church, with the force of the explosion causing widespread panic.Emergency responders and residents rushed to help those caught in the blast, as the scale of the destruction became clear in the aftermath.Temascalcingo, a municipality with about 66,000 residents, was hosting hundreds of people for the religious celebrations when the explosion occurred.The incident has once again highlighted the dangers posed by pyrotechnics in Mexico, where fireworks are widely used during street celebrations, religious festivals and other public gatherings.Similar accidents have occurred in the country before. Nearly four years ago, a powerful fireworks explosion in a village in the municipality of Huejutla, in the central state of Hidalgo, left 17 people injured.
Article Summary: At least 10 people were killed and 64 injured in the explosion in Temascalcingo. Residents were gathered to watch a fireworks display as part of celebrations for the local patron saint. The explosion brought down the walls of surrounding buildings and triggered a fire in the town square.

Article Title: Video captures moment Amazon cargo plane hurtles off runway, erupts in flames
Article Text:
Five people were killed in the crash, while another five were injured

Huge emergency response as flights disrupted

An Amazon Prime Air cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday afternoon, striking multiple vehicles and bursting into flames in a deadly crash that killed at least five people and injured five others.The Boeing 767-300, operating as Amazon Prime Air Flight 7598 and operated by cargo carrier 21 Air, had arrived from San Juan, Puerto Rico, when the aircraft ran off the runway shortly before 2pm local time.Dramatic footage showed the plane racing beyond the runway before crashing through an area used by warehouse workers and other businesses surrounding the airport. Thick black smoke and flames could be seen rising from the aircraft as emergency crews rushed to the scene.The plane eventually came to rest beside a roadway near two semi-trucks. Images showed the aircraft largely intact but resting on its belly and engulfed in flames.Five people were killed in the crash, while another five were injured. Three of the injured were in critical condition, according to Miami-Dade County officials. It was initially unclear whether the pilots survived or whether all those killed were in vehicles struck by the aircraft.Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Chief Ray Jadallah said the pilot and co-pilot were trapped inside the cockpit following the crash, while some people were also trapped in vehicles. Crews had to rescue a person who was pinned beneath a vehicle.More than 60 Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units and around 200 emergency personnel responded as firefighters battled an intense fire involving the aircraft. Specialised airport firefighting units used foam to extinguish the flames, while crews continued dealing with a fuel leak several hours after the crash.The accident brought operations at the busy airport to a halt for much of Sunday afternoon, with more than 160 flights cancelled and nearly 325 delayed by late in the day. Some flights were also diverted to Orlando International Airport.The cause of the crash remains unknown and is being investigated by the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board, which sent a team led by its chairwoman, Jennifer Homendy, to Miami.Weather conditions may also form part of the investigation, with thunderstorms and wind gusts of up to 30 mph recorded in the area around the time of the crash.Aviation experts have raised questions about the aircraft's landing. Former United Airlines pilot Steve Arroyo said investigators would need to establish whether the plane touched down within the designated landing zone and, if not, why the crew did not abort the landing and attempt another approach.Former Transportation Department inspector general Mary Schiavo, meanwhile, said video of the landing appeared to show the aircraft floating above the runway for an extended period before touching down, potentially leaving insufficient runway to stop safely.
Article Summary: Boeing 767-300 ran off the runway at Miami International Airport. It struck multiple vehicles and burst into flames before coming to rest. Five people were killed in the crash, while another five were injured. More than 160 flights were cancelled and nearly 325 delayed by late in the day.

Article Title: Suspected drones near Amritsar airport trigger flight diversions, security alert
Article Text:

AMRITSAR: Suspected drone-like objects were reportedly spotted near Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport late on Sunday night, triggering a major security alert and leading to the diversion of seven incoming flights as a precautionary measure.Anirudh Sharma, who holds the additional charge of Airport Director, confirmed that drone-like objects were noticed in the vicinity of the airport. Following the alert, two incoming flights were diverted to Chandigarh and five to Delhi. Airport operations remained suspended from 9.50 pm to 11.15 pm, he said.Sources said the suspected flying objects were seen outside the airport's perimeter wall, following which Air Traffic Control (ATC) suspended landing operations due to concerns over the safety of aircraft operating in the area.Sources said the police suspect that the drones were flown locally.The incident is being viewed seriously, particularly because the international airport is located close to the India-Pakistan border. Security agencies were immediately alerted, while the matter was also reported to the police for investigation.Sources said the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), responsible for airport security, has also heightened its vigilance following the incidentWhile the exact nature and origin of the suspected objects are yet to be established, investigators are examining all possibilities.Sources did not rule out the possibility that locally operated drones may have entered the restricted airspace near the airport.However, given the increasing instances of drones allegedly being used from across the Pakistan border to smuggle narcotics, arms and ammunition into Punjab, security agencies are also examining whether there could be a cross-border angle, sources said.Sharma said the matter had been reported to the police, who are now investigating the incident to determine whether the suspicious flying objects were actually drones or some other objects and where they were flown from.
Article Summary: Two incoming flights were diverted to Chandigarh and five to Delhi. Airport operations remained suspended from 9.50 pm to 11.15 pm. Police suspect that the drones were flown locally. The incident is being viewed seriously, particularly because the international airport is located close to the India-Pakistan border.

Article Title: 40 years old building, 'illegal' work, waterlogged basement: The many holes in Satya Niketan's collapsed PG
Article Text:
A building collapsed in Satya Niketan, prompting an investigation into its structural integrity.

Amid Screams Of Help, Locals & Students Form Human Chain In Early Rescue At Satya Niketan
