NEW DELHI: Investigators are probing if construction work might have been carried out illegally in the basement of the building in Satya Niketan when it collapsed Sunday.Initial inquiries suggested the basement used to get waterlogged, which may have weakened the structure, and the construction work may have aggravated the situation and contributed to the tragedy. MCD said it was looking into the matter.Police are likely to examine how permission for the work was given during the monsoon season, sources said. “The building owner, contractor and labourers will be interrogated,” an investigator said.It was unclear whether the building owner had obtained permission for the construction or whether it was being carried out illegally, allegedly in connivance with local authorities, which are supposed to flag such activities.Mayor Pravesh Wahi, who inspected the site, said the building was more than four decades old and had two rooms on each floor in a ground-plus-four-storey structure. “MCD’s immediate priority is the rescue operation. It is too early to determine whether any construction or repair work was underway when the building collapsed, as the entire structure was buried under debris,” he said, adding that 13 students were registered as paying guests in the building.According to an MCD official, “No record of booking or sealing is available and no complaints have been received of any work in this property.”A senior MCD official said the building violated the prescribed height limit of 17.5 metres. However, he added, the civic body was yet to ascertain whether any digging or structural work was recently carried out in the basement or ground floor. “Given the incessant rain, we are examining the possibility of seepage weakening the structure. Repair or other work could also have contributed to the collapse. At this stage, however, it is difficult to establish the exact cause,” he said.The official said the building owner, who lives in Gurgaon, has another property in the area. “There is negligence on his part. The adjoining building was also found to have structural deficiencies, including the absence of a proper beam structure. Considering the safety risk, the neighbouring building has been vacated and will be demolished Monday. The residents will be shifted to a nearby community hall,” he said.According to former DFS director Atul Garg, “There is still not much clarity regarding PG accommodations. If they are above 15 metres, the rules are defined. For buildings below 15 metres, the fire brigade does not grant approval. This building was built for residential purposes, but it was being used for commercial purposes. The building authority is responsible in this case.”Rescue operation under way at the site
Article Summary: Police likely to examine how permission for the work was given during the monsoon season. Investigators probing if construction work might have been carried out illegally in the basement of the building in Satya Niketan. Initial inquiries suggest the basement used to get waterlogged, which may have weakened the structure.

Article Title: ‘Ground shook, we thought it was a quake’: Screams of help, locals and students form human chain in early rescue at Satya Niketan
Article Text:
(Photo credit: Tarun Rawat/TNN ) Rescue operation underway after a building collapsed at Satya Niketan area, in New Delhi on Sunday

Cloud of dust,panic and students under rubble





NEW DELHI: There was a cushion between a student’s face and a concrete slab that he was under. The rest of the youth’s body was pinned under the debris. Local people were desperately trying to lift a heavy block of concrete to free him.“1, 2, 3, uthaaa.” the rescuers yelled, hoping to give each other and the youth a boost. But the slab was too heavy to be lifted at once.At the building collapse site at Satya Niketan, scenes like this one were visible everywhere. Residents, students and rescuers were trying whatever was in their power to save lives.“When the structure collapsed, students started to immediately clear the debris. The ones who were trapped were screaming ‘bachao, bachao humein’. 6-7 students have been rescued by now, more are trapped inside,” said Rajiv Kumar (42).There was a human chain of hands clearing the debris. Some residents had ordered oxygen cylinders from quick commerce apps for those trapped under the rubble. Locals attempted to pump the oxygen through gaps in the debris to help the students breathe and prevent suffocation from dust, while waiting for heavy machinery to arrive and move the heavy slabs of concrete.The human chain also cleared the path of rubble so that the rescue work would not slow down.To the residents, the collapse felt like an earthquake. “We felt the ground shake. When we ran outside, we saw that a house had completely collapsed,” said Roshan Pal, a student from Lucknow.“When I came out, a cloud of dust was spreading in all directions. That’s when we realised that the building had collapsed. We started removing one part of a wall soon after. Seven students were pinned under it,” said Rahul Gaur, a resident.University of Delhi South Campus director, professor Rajni Abbi, said the university was trying to ascertain how many students lived in the Satya Niketan building. “The exact number of people inside the collapsed building is not known yet. We have informed all colleges and asked them to assess how many of their students are residing in Satya Niketan,” Abbi said.She said colleges had also been asked to ensure the safety of students living in the area and call them back to their respective campuses. “A call was received from inside the debris, and there has also been a video call from within. Our prime concern is that the children come out safely,” she said.Ram, a resident, said the collapse happened around 1.20 pm. “NDRF arrived first, with 11–12 personnel,” he added.The building had no pillars, the resident said. "In the Satya Niketan area, many houses do not have pillars. These are old buildings, constructed when Satya Niketan was first developed, and floors have since been added to these structures. In the building that collapsed, some work was on in the basement. Water had accumulated there,” he said.Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) president Aryan Maan said: “I arrived within ten minutes, assembling ABVP volunteers from South Campus to dig through the rubble and help evacuate survivors.”Teams from NSUI and AISA also came. NSUI president Vinod Jakhar rushed to the spot after learning that an organisation member was trapped inside the structure. “I reached as soon as I could and found an absence of immediate civic administration, police, or fire response. Student volunteers manually hauled away concrete slabs, managing to pull three victims out, saving two lives. One resident had died.”Student groups immediately transformed their digital networks into emergency lifelines, circulating helpline numbers across social media.Multiple vehicles were also crushed.
Article Summary: Residents, students and rescuers were trying whatever was in their power to save lives. Student groups immediately transformed their digital networks into emergency lifelines. Student volunteers manually hauled away concrete slabs, managing to pull three victims out, saving two lives. One resident had died.

Article Title: Delhi Boy Death: Delhi Teen Dies After Alleged Electrocution in Waterlogged Lane
Article Text:
A 13-year-old boy Kaushal





NEW DELHI: A 13-year-old boy was found unconscious in a waterlogged lane in west Delhi ’s Bindapur and later died Friday. His family has alleged that he died because he was electrocuted when he touched an iron pipe near an electricity pole.Kaushal was a Class 8 student of Sarvodaya Vidyalaya in Janakpuri and lived in Nand Ram Park, Bindapur. Police said information about the boy’s death came from BM Gupta Hospital to the Bindapur police station on Sept 4.The cops said Kaushal’s grandmother, Sridevi, found him unconscious about 50 metres from their home. She alerted his mother, Hemlata, who rushed him to the hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead. His body was shifted to DDU Hospital, where a postmortem was conducted Saturday.The family said the boy was walking through the waterlogged lane after heavy rain when a motorcycle passed by, rather close to him. Fearing he would fall, he allegedly grabbed an iron pipe attached to the electricity pole. The family and residents said the pipe emitted an electric shock that killed him. Locals reportedly pulled the boy away using a wooden stick, but he could not be saved.A senior police officer said the exact reason for his death will be established in the postmortem. Police are examining the circumstances surrounding it.Kaushal has a six-year-old sister. His father works at an optical shop in Rama Garden, while his mother is a homemaker.The family alleged that persistent waterlogging and electrical safety issues in the locality contributed to the boy’s death.Residents also claimed that the lane frequently remained waterlogged even after light rainfall and that sewage water accumulated there even when it was not raining. They said that had the lane not been flooded, Kaushal would not have needed to hold the pipe to prevent himself from falling.Police said further action would be taken after the postmortem and completion of the inquiry.
Article Summary: Kaushal was a Class 8 student of Sarvodaya Vidyalaya in Janakpuri and lived in Nand Ram Park, Bindapur. His family said the boy was walking through the waterlogged lane after heavy rain when a motorcycle passed by, rather close to him. Fearing he would fall, he allegedly grabbed an iron pipe attached to the electricity pole.

Article Title: Use of DJs during festivals ‘down’ in Mumbai; Pune holds rally against ‘noise’
Article Text:
Hundreds of Pune residents marched from Bal Gandharva Chowk to the PMC headquarters to protest against high-decibel levels during festival celebrations





PUNE: Hundreds of residents from across the city on Sunday took to the streets to oppose the use of DJs and loudspeakers during festivals. United under the ‘Punekars Against Loudspeakers’ banner, they carried out a protest march from Bal Gandharva Chowk to Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) headquarters in Shivajinagar. “We are not against any festival, but stand against loud noise, speakers and DJs for celebrations,” said several protesters.The agitators waved placards and shouted slogans in support of a loudspeaker ban amid heavy police bandobast set up in place for the rally. The citizens also presented a memorandum to the police department outlining their demands. These included pre-event on-site inspections and pre-event officer accountability, proactive seizures of equipment violating norms, acoustic and technical justifications, real-time decibel tracking, a public nodal officer directory, and a daily action register.“We want illegal, deafening loudspeakers and similar health-hazardous noise-polluting instruments and equipment to be banned, not only during Ganeshotsav but across all types of religious, caste, and political processions and celebrations,” said Rahul Sawant, a medical practitioner present at the march.According to representatives, in light of clear directives from Supreme Court and National Green Tribunal (NGT), they have appealed to the police commissionerate, PMC and Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) to establish a joint operating protocol for proactive inspections.“Police commissioners in other cities are issuing prohibitions in this regard. If traditions are respected in Solapur and the law is upheld in Nagpur, why is there free rein in Pune? Why has Solapur succeeded and Nagpur managed noise-free loudspeakers, while Pune remains stuck?” said Umesh Khandare, another participant.Protesters of all ages attended Sunday’s march, from youngsters to senior citizens.Participant Vidya Kelkar said, “I am 82 years old. Having seen so many Ganesh festivals over my lifetime, I feel the event has taken a very troubling turn in recent years. For people like us, the sound of the DJs makes our window panes rattle, even when closed. Because of this, proper sleep and rest have become impossible. What are we supposed to do?”“We all witnessed it during Dahi Handi. The police had set restrictions and carried out their duty diligently by confiscating speakers. But why should the police even need to step in and take such action? If you want to celebrate a festival within acceptable limits, respect those limits. Since people fail to do so, a total ban is the only solution,” said protester Kirti Limaye.Police said that around 350-400 people joined the rally. “We have received their memorandum of demands. Due legal action will be taken,” deputy commissioner of police (DCP) Krushikesh Rawale told reporters.
Article Summary: Hundreds of Pune residents marched from Bal Gandharva Chowk to the PMC headquarters to protest against high-decibel levels during festival celebrations. They waved placards and shouted slogans in support of a loudspeaker ban amid heavy police bandobast set up in place for the rally.

Article Title: Injured govindas advised CT scans, Shiv Sena men assault Palghar hospital staffer
Article Text:
The Sainiks also entered the ICU & general ward, removed IV lines & took away the 5 injured govindas

By- Suhas.Birhade





PALGHAR: Some Shiv Sena workers allegedly assaulted an employee of a private hospital in Palghar, abused doctors and threatened to damage property early on Sunday after being told that five govindas injured during a dahi handi celebration needed to undergo CT scans.Sena’s district chief Kundan Sankhe claimed they went to Relief Hospital after receiving complaints that the govindas were not being allowed to leave and were being asked to settle the bill, which was to be covered by the party. He said a dispute arose after hospital staffers failed to give satisfactory answers.Palghar police filed a case under various sections against 17 persons, including Rohit Gavit, son of Sena MLA Rajendra Gavit and the party’s deputy taluka chief, Sankhe, and the city Sena chief. The assault was captured on a CCTV camera in the hospital’s reception. Kishor Manbhav, senior inspector, said police examined the CCTV footage and launched a search for the accused.The assault came two months after Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre and his aides allegedly assaulted medical staffers of a Dombivli hospital purportedly over delay in treating a pregnant patient.Around 1.15am on Sunday, Sena’s district chief Kundan Sankhe, its city chief Rahul Gharat and other workers allegedly entered Relief Hospital in Palghar, questioning doctors over the treatment and the need for the injured govindas to undergo CT scans.A woman doctor working near the reception reportedly explained that the scans were necessary because the patients had suffered head injuries.The Sena workers allegedly became angry, threatened to damage hospital property and abused doctors. Gharat then allegedly slapped the receptionist, Vivek Zinga (23). The assault was caught on camera.The workers then allegedly entered the ICU, removed the intravenous fluid lines of govindas, and took all five of them away from the hospital.Sena had organised a dahi handi celebration on Saturday, during which the five govindas were injured. Three were in the ICU with head injuries and two in the general ward. Their bill had reached Rs 19,866, of which a Sena worker had paid Rs 10,000, with the remaining amount reportedly to be paid by the party’s district chief.The hospital administration said Sankhe questioned why the patients had been admitted to the ICU and why the bill was so high, and intimidated and assaulted the staff. “Our entire staff is frightened. The employee who was assaulted is under stress. Strict action should be taken against all those who assaulted him,” said the hospital’s Dr Vishal Kotgirkar.Sections 115(2) (causing hurt), 351(2) and 352 (insulting and threatening with the intention of causing a breach of peace), 329(4) (criminal trespass), and 189(1), 189(2) and 190 (unlawful assembly), as well as Sections 3 and 4 of Maharashtra Medicare Service Persons and Medicare Service Institutions Act, 2010, relating to assault on medical personnel, violent acts and damage to hospital property, have been invoked in the case.The Boisar unit of Indian Medical Association, represented by president Dr Milan Kamat and secretary Dr Prakash Babu, expressed concern over the attack and sought appropriate preventive measures to ensure the safety and security of the hospital and its staffers.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena workers allegedly assaulted an employee of a private hospital in Palghar, abused doctors and threatened to damage property. The workers entered the ICU, removed the intravenous fluid lines of govindas, and took all five of them away from the hospital. The assault was captured on a CCTV camera in the hospital’s reception. Police filed a case under various sections against 17 persons.

Article Title: Mystery email claims BHU doctor assaulted ‘Doctor God’ inside hospital, institute denies
Article Text:
Prof TK Lahiri





VARANASI: An email alleging that emeritus professor of Institute of Medical Sciences-BHU and Padma Shri awardee TK Lahiri (85) was beaten up by a doctor at the super-speciality ward of SSL Hospital, where he has been admitted since Jan 27, prompted the hospital authorities to swing into action.Lahiri, popularly known as “Doctor God”, retired from IMS-BHU in 2003, but continues to provide free medical consultation to patients.As photographs of Lahiri showing marks of injury on his cheek and blood clot in one of his eyes went viral on social media, the authorities constituted a medical board to probe the allegations. Based on the board’s report, the hospital’s medical superintendent, Dr Punit, termed the allegations of assault or misconduct against Lahiri baseless.Posing as Lahiri’s relative, the mailer blamed a doctor for allegedly assaulting and abusing him inside the ward where he is being treated in the super-speciality block of SSL Hospital.Taking note of the allegations, BHU said in an official statement that after receiving the email, vice-chancellor Prof Ajit Kumar Chaturvedi, Institute of Medical Sciences-BHU director Prof SN Sankhwar and Dr Punit swung into action.Dr Punit said that after receiving the email, he and the IMS-BHU director visited Lahiri in the ward and enquired about his health. On Sept 3, the MS ordered a comprehensive examination of Lahiri by specialists from cardiology, general medicine, psychiatry, geriatrics, neurology, critical care, and tuberculosis and chest diseases.According to the specialists’ reports, Lahiri is suffering from age-related physical and mental health conditions, including heart disease, tuberculosis-related ailments, senile dementia and behavioural changes. Due to these conditions, Lahiri sometimes shows reluctance regarding treatment, daily routine and personal hygiene, mentioned the varsity.He was admitted to Sir Sunderlal Hospital on Jan 27, with chest-related complaints and has since been under continuous care and treatment by doctors and hospital staff. Since his admission, Dr Punit said BHU administration tried contacting his family members to update them regarding his health, but no relative came forward for his care so far.The IMS director and medical superintendent continue to monitor his health and visited him again in the ward on Sunday, claimed the vasrity.Lahiri regularly walks from home to the super speciality block OPD. Lahiri, revered for his dedication to service, is known for donating a large part of his pension, refusing assistance and teaching generations of students. He is also a familiar figure on campus, often seen heading to his workplace from the VC Lodge in his apron, carrying an umbrella in one hand and a black bag in the other. He was awarded the Padma Sri in 2016 in recognition of his contribution to society and the medical profession.
Article Summary: An email alleging that emeritus professor TK Lahiri (85) was beaten up by a doctor at the super-speciality ward of SSL Hospital prompted the hospital authorities to swing into action. Lahiri, popularly known as ‘Doctor God’, retired from IMS-BHU in 2003, but continues to provide free medical consultation to patients.

Article Title: Row over DJs during festivals in Maharashtra: Shiv Sena minister backs ‘sound,’ 2 other mantris want it shut out
Article Text:
MNS chief Raj Thackeray and NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule questioned why DJ music could be banned in Nagpur and not in Pune.





MUMBAI: The debate over use of DJs during festivals, especially Ganeshotsav, in Maharashtra, intensified on Sunday with Shiv Sena’s Yogesh Kadam, minister of state in the home department, saying “sound” during Hindu festivals will not stop, and his cabinet colleagues Sanjay Shirsat (also of Sena) and Meghana Bordikar (BJP) striking a different note by making a strong pitch against use of DJ sound systems.State culture minister Ashish Shelar on Sunday backed what CM Devendra Fadnavis had said on Friday, saying it is for the local administration and residents to stop use of DJs.Fadnavis had said that the state government was working to build a consensus on restricting the use of high-decibel DJ systems during festivals and called for a return to traditional ways of celebrating.On Sunday, Pune residents held a rally, demanding a blanket ban on use of DJs during festivals, religious events and anniversary celebrations to help curb noise pollution, while criticising the inaction of the state govt and police.MNS chief Raj Thackeray and NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule questioned why DJ music could be banned in Nagpur and not in Pune.Kadam said that sound during Hindu festivals would not stop. “Festivals are not celebrated like this (without sound). This is the stand of Shiv Sena and the government,” he said at a dahi handi event on Saturday. “I said this firmly in Pune on Friday, and I am saying this in Mumbai.”The demand for festivals free of DJs and high-powered loudspeakers has been gaining momentum in the state, with Pune activist Vidyanad Bapat emerging as one of the prominent voices opposing the use of high-decibel sound systems that cause noise pollution during festivities.Minister of state for health Bordikar and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district guardian minister Shirsat stressed the importance of adhering to noise pollution norms.Bordikar emphasised that while festivals should be celebrated with enthusiasm, they must not cause distress or health hazards to others. “Unfortunately, my cousin died because of a DJ system last year. We repeatedly appeal to people, and Supreme Court has also laid down guidelines, but many fail to adhere to them. The use of DJs can lead to fatal consequences, and I have experienced this personal tragedy myself,” she said.Echoing her concerns, Shirsat said that the administration in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and police will strictly enforce noise regulations, urging organisers to celebrate with traditional music instead of DJs.Last week, Mumbai Police commissioner Deven Bharati held a meeting with representatives of all Sarvajanik Ganesh mandals in the city. It was acknowledged at the meeting that in the last 8-10 years, the use of DJ music and laser lights has come down significantly across Mumbai.Naresh Dahibavkar, president of Brihanmumbai Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Samanvay Samiti, said it is a mix of decisions and actions by NGOs and authorities that have ensured nearly 80% of DJ music and laser lights being replaced with traditional instruments.“It was in 2016 that Mahesh Bedekar filed a PIL against mandaps and noise pollution. The court made it mandatory that noise levels cannot exceed 55dB during daytime and 45dB between 10pm and 6 am. And there was proper implementation,” said Dahibavkar.At every meeting before the festival, mandals are apprised about the repercussions of causing noise pollution as well as the harmful effects on health, he added.Sumaira Abdulali, convener, NGO Awaaz Foundation said there has been a ban on DJs since 2018, and it has changed the character of the festival.“Ganesh mandals have done it successfully and it shows that if they cooperate, noise pollution can be controlled. However, mandals need to look into the use of loudspeakers. While traditional instruments have replaced DJ music, the loudspeakers amply the sound by at least 20-40%. The use of loudspeakers must be stopped,” said Abdulali.
Article Summary: The debate over use of DJs during festivals, especially Ganeshotsav, in Maharashtra, intensified on Sunday. Shiv Sena’s Yogesh Kadam, minister of state in the home department, said “sound’ during Hindu festivals will not stop. State culture minister Ashish Shelar on Sunday backed what CM Devendra Fadnavis had said.

Article Title: Won’t speak on Ajit’s death from now, says Supriya Sule
Article Text:
Supriya Sule will no longer discuss Ajit Pawar's accident. She stated continued talk creates misunderstandings among the public

Enforce SC curbs across state, don’t be selective

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think about the use of DJs during festivals like Ganeshotsav and Diwali? It enhances the festive spirit. It causes noise pollution and disturbance. It should be allowed within decibel limits. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NAGPUR: NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule on Sunday signalled she would stop commenting on the ongoing discussion around the accident on Jan 28 near Baramati airport that claimed the life of her cousin, deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar , saying continued talk on the subject was creating misunderstandings among people.Sule said, "I will not speak on Ajit Pawar's accident going forward. There is continuous discussion on this issue, which is creating many misunderstandings. Therefore, with folded hands, my request is that I have stopped speaking on this topic from today." She did not elaborate further and declined to take additional questions on the matter.Sule on Sunday said the state govt should implement Supreme Court’s 10pm cut-off for DJs uniformly across Maharashtra instead of imposing an outright ban in some cities and looking away elsewhere.On the controversy over playing DJs and loudspeakers, Sule said, “The matter has escalated. I would urge the govt to develop a consensus as there are big festivals like Ganeshotsav, Navratri and then Diwali. We need to sensibly bring all sections of society together and find a way forward.”Supporters of DJ have claimed students themselves are dancing in processions, “hence using them as a shield to impose a ban isn’t justified”. Sule drew a distinction. “There is no objection to dancing or to what anyone wants to do. The objection is about implementation. What does the Supreme Court’s order say? There is an order on decibel limit and that DJs must be shut off after 10pm,” she said.Citing the example of Nagpur, where police claimed to have ensured that noise limits were not breached, Sule said options that could fit within rules should be explored.
Article Summary: NCP MP Supriya Sule will no longer discuss Ajit Pawar's accident. She stated continued talk creates misunderstandings among the public. Sule said the state govt should implement Supreme Court’s 10pm cut-off for DJs uniformly across Maharashtra.

Article Title: UP head cop held for bludgeoning wife to death with iron rod, motive unclear
Article Text:
The victim Rashmi Srivastava, wife of head constable Himanshu





LUCKNOW: A 40-year-old police head constable was arrested on Sunday for allegedly killing his wife by repeatedly striking her on the head with an iron rod at their rented accommodation in the Paper Mill area of Mahanagar.The victim, identified as Rashmi Srivastava (38), died on the spot after sustaining grievous head injuries. The accused, Himanshu Srivastava (40), a 2011-batch head constable posted in the office of the Joint Commissioner of Police (Law and Order), Lucknow, has been taken into custody and is being questioned. He worked in the Right to Information cell.According to police, the incident came to light around 2.30 pm when the landlord alerted the police control room. A police team rushed to the spot and found Rashmi lying in a pool of blood inside the house. Preliminary investigation suggests that Himanshu allegedly attacked his wife multiple times with an iron rod, inflicting fatal injuries. However, the motive behind the killing remains unclear. “It is not clear why he attacked his wife. The matter is being investigated,” said Akhilesh Mishra, SHO, Mahanagar. Police said Himanshu is a native of Ayodhya, while Rashmi hailed from Ambedkar Nagar district.DCP (Central) Vikrant Vir said an FIR has been registered against the accused on a complaint lodged by the victim’s brother Saurabh Srivastava. “The accused constable is in custody and is being questioned. Further legal action is being taken,” he said.
Article Summary: Rashmi Srivastava, 38, died on the spot after sustaining grievous head injuries. Her husband Himanshu, 40, is a 2011-batch head constable posted in the office of the Joint Commissioner of Police (Law and Order), Lucknow.

Article Title: 4 killed, over two dozen injured as bus overturns after hitting divider in UP's Baghpat
Article Text:
Four pilgrims died when their bus overturned on the Eastern Peripheral Expressway early Monday





BAGHPAT: At least four people were killed and over two dozen injured when a passenger bus hit a road divider and overturned on the Eastern Peripheral Expressway in UP’s Baghpat district early Monday, police said.The bus was carrying 32 people from Rajasthan to Budaun.The accident took place at around 12.30 am in the Khekra police station area.Following the incident, four Police Response Vehicles (PRVs) under Dial 112, along with ambulances and personnel from the Khekra police station, reached the spot and began rescue operations, Superintendent of Police Suraj Rai said.The injured were taken to Community Health Centres in Khekra and Baghpat, as well as the district hospital in Baghpat. Those with serious injuries were later referred to higher medical centres for specialised treatment.Police said four people had died in the accident so far, while efforts were underway to establish their identities.Authorities are also contacting the relatives of those killed and injured and providing them with the necessary assistance.The police have asked family members looking for information about the deceased or injured to contact Baghpat Police on 9454417383.
Article Summary: Bus was carrying 32 people from Rajasthan to Budaun. Accident took place at around 12.30 am in the Khekra police station area. Those with serious injuries were later referred to higher medical centres for specialised treatment.

Article Title: 4 months after marriage, couple found dead in Kerala Lake
Article Text:
The deceased couple Rajeev, 26 and Abhirami, 19





THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: A newlywed couple was found dead in Sasthamcotta Lake near Ambalakkadavu, Kollam, on Sunday morning, with police suspecting suicide. The deceased have been identified as Rajeev, 26 and Abhirami, 19, a resident of Sasthamcotta.According to police, Abhirami’s body was first spotted near Ambalakkadavu early Sunday morning. Following the discovery, a search operation was launched by the Sasthamcotta fire and rescue personnel. Rajeev’s body was subsequently recovered from the lake, around 50 metres from where Abhirami’s body had been found.Police suspect that the couple entered the lake in the early hours of Sunday. However, the exact circumstances that led to their deaths are yet to be established.Rajeev and Abhirami had been in a relationship before getting married around four months ago. Their marriage was reportedly solemnised despite strong opposition from both families. Following the marriage, the couple had been staying in a rented house.According to relatives and police, the couple had maintained little or no contact with their respective families after the marriage.Rajeev was working as a cleaning staff member at Ambalamkunnu school.Police said the couple had been summoned to the Puyappally police station last month for counselling. The reason for the couple’s decision to end their lives, however, remains unclear.The bodies were kept at the Sasthamcotta taluk hospital mortuary and were later handed over to relatives.Sasthamcotta Police have registered a case and launched an investigation to ascertain the circumstances leading to the deaths. Police will also gather information from relatives and other persons who had been in contact with the couple in recent days.
Article Summary: Rajeev, 26 and Abhirami, 19, were found dead in Sasthamcotta Lake, Kollam. Police suspect that the couple entered the lake in the early hours of Sunday. The reason for the couple's decision to end their lives, however, remains unclear.

Article Title: Out on bail in attempt to murder case, UP man rapes dalit minor
Article Text:
(Representative of image) The accused had a dispute with a youth from his village in 2022.

(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)





AGRA: A 25-year-old man, who walked out of jail on bail about a year ago in an “attempt to murder” case, has been re-arrested for raping a 16-year-old Dalit girl at a farm on Sept 3.Police said on Sunday that the man allegedly took her to a secluded place and sexually assaulted her. Based on a complaint, an FIR was registered at the local thana under BNS sections 65 (1) ( rape ) and 351 (criminal intimidation) along with the SC/ST Act and Pocso Act SP (Mathura-rural), Suresh Chandra Rawat, said the accused had a dispute with a youth from his village in 2022. “During that incident, he gouged out both his eyes with his fingers. A case was subsequently registered at Jait police station under IPC 307 (attempt to murder), and he was sent to jail.”According to police, the accused secured bail after spending around three years in custody.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old man, who walked out of jail on bail about a year ago in an ‘attempt to murder’ case, has been re-arrested. The man allegedly took her to a secluded place and sexually assaulted her. The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy.

Article Title: 'Head in fridge, fingers cut off': Woman murdered in Guwahati flat; husband surrenders
Article Text:
A 25-year-old married woman was allegedly murdered in Guwahati's Basisthapur area (Picture credits:X)

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the portrayal of domestic violence in media effective in raising awareness? Very Effective Not Very Effective 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(With agency inputs).





GUWAHATI: A 25-year-old married woman was allegedly murdered, with her severed head found packed in a polythene bag inside a refrigerator at a flat in Assam’s Basisthapur area in Guwahati, officials said on Monday.The victim has been identified as Riya Talukdar Goswami. Investigators described the killing as extremely brutal, saying the accused allegedly severed her head, placed it inside a polythene bag and stored it in the refrigerator. Her fingers were also allegedly cut off.According to news agency ANI, Anurag Sharma, ADCP (East) of Guwahati Police Commissionerate, confirmed that Riya’s husband, Ramanujan Goswami, is the prime accused in the case. He surrendered before police and confessed to the crime.A senior police official said preliminary investigations suggest that the crime took place around 48 hours before the body was discovered.Riya and Ramanujan had married around six months ago and were residing together in the flat, according to reports.Police recovered the victim’s body on Sunday night after neighbours alerted authorities about a foul smell emanating from the apartment. Investigating teams also seized a weapon from the premises, which is suspected to have been used in the crime.The body was subsequently sent to Guwahati Medical College & Hospital (GMCH) for post-mortem examination.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old married woman was allegedly murdered, with her severed head found packed in a polythene bag inside a refrigerator at a flat in Assam’s Basisthapur area in Guwahati. The victim has been identified as Riya Talukdar Goswami. Investigators described the killing as extremely brutal, saying the accused allegedly severed her head.

Article Title: Police hits drug trade where it hurts most, targets traffickers’ ill-gotten wealth
Article Text:
Charkhi Dadri Police intensified its crackdown on drug traffickers and their assets.





CHARKHI DADRI: Charkhi Dadri Police has intensified its crackdown on drug traffickers, targeting not only those allegedly involved in the illegal narcotics trade but also the properties, valuables and other assets believed to have been acquired from its proceeds.Acting on the strict directions of Superintendent of Police Logesh Kumar P., the district police is conducting a special campaign aimed at making Charkhi Dadri drug-free. As part of the drive, police are taking legal action against alleged drug traffickers while simultaneously tightening the noose around their suspected ill-gotten wealth.Over Friday and Saturday, police teams conducted raids at premises linked to three alleged drug traffickers in Pichopa Kalan, Jewali and Mehra villages and carried out seizure action under Section 68F of the NDPS Act.on Friday, a Badhra police team led by SI Pawan, along with PSI Harender, in-charge of Atela Kalan police post, raided premises linked to Sunil, son of Balwan, of Pichopa Kalan, and Hardeep, son of Bhup Singh, of Jewali. On Saturday, a Jhojhu Kalan police team led by ASI Surender Mohan conducted action at the premises of Kulbir, son of Maturam, in Mehra.Police said luxury household articles and valuable items allegedly acquired from drug-trafficking proceeds were seized as part of the prescribed legal proceedings.With the latest action, 24 premises linked to alleged drug traffickers have been subjected to effective action under Section 68F in Charkhi Dadri during 2026, police said.SP Logesh Kumar said the force was following a “zero-tolerance” policy against drug trafficking and would continue targeting the financial foundations of the illegal trade. He said the objective was not merely to put traffickers behind bars but also to dismantle the illegal wealth allegedly built at the cost of the future of young people.The SP appealed to residents to share information regarding the sale, supply or trafficking of narcotic substances and suspicious activities. Police assured that the identity of informants would be kept completely confidential and strict legal action would follow against those involved in the illegal drug trade.
Article Summary: Charkhi Dadri Police has intensified its crackdown on drug traffickers and their assets. Police are taking legal action against alleged drug traffickers while simultaneously tightening the noose around their suspected ill-gotten wealth. Police teams conducted raids at premises linked to three alleged drug. traffickers in Pichopa Kalan, Jewali and Mehra.

Article Title: A popular DM, a sudden exit, an unanswered question
Article Text:
Divya Mittal voluntarily resigned from the IAS after a thirteen-year career.

Why Her Exit Stunned Many

Popular, but sometimes at odds

From London to the IAS

Did she hit a plateau?

What comes next?





Today, I voluntarily resigned from the IAS, bringing an unforgettable 13-year journey to a close.” With those words, Divya Mittal announced on social media on Sunday that she was walking away from the civil services. The resignation of the 43-year-old, 2013-batch Uttar Pradesh-cadre officer, who was serving as special secretary in the revenue department, is yet to be formally accepted.Mittal has not disclosed why she quit, telling TOI that she will reveal her plans at the appropriate time. Her farewell post instead retraced her journey from IIT-Delhi and IIM-Bangalore to a job in London, and then back to India to repay what she called a “debt to this soil”.Her decision surprised colleagues and admirers because Mittal had acquired a public following unusual for a bureaucrat. In Mirzapur and Deoria, she became known as an accessible, hands-on administrator who used social media to communicate her work.Her best-known initiative brought piped water to Lahuriya Deh, a remote hilltop hamlet whose residents had long depended on tankers and water collected from pits.In her farewell note, Mittal recalled an elderly woman silently touching her head and blessing her when water reached the village.Village representatives also remember “Mera Gaon, Mera Gaurav”, a WhatsApp group connecting more than 800 pradhans with district officials. Mittal would tag officials when problems were raised and monitor the response, effectively giving village heads a direct line to the administration.Those who worked with her describe two distinct sides to her administrative personality. She was soft-spoken and approachable with members of the public, but could lose her temper in official meetings when instructions were ignored. Her willingness to take decisions independently won her admirers, but it did not always make for easy relations with elected representatives.The completion of the Lahuriya Deh water project itself became a source of friction. Mittal performed the “jal puja” when water reached the village, but elected representatives were absent. Critics accused her of sidelining politicians; her supporters saw an administrator more interested in finishing the work than managing political optics.She was transferred from Mirzapur soon after the event and remained without a posting for several months.There had been confrontations earlier, too. During her tenure as Sant Kabir Nagar DM, Mittal found herself at odds with then district minister-in-charge Ashish Patel, husband of Union minister and Mirzapur MP Anupriya Patel, after she sent a representative to receive him instead of attending personally. As Deoria DM, differences during a District Development Coordination and Monitoring Committee meeting also generated controversy.Her visibility added another layer to the friction. In Deoria, she came to be known as the “reel wali DM” due to her frequent social-media posts on govt initiatives, community events and public outreach. Supporters saw it as an effort to make the administration more accessible. Detractors questioned whether the officer’s public profile was beginning to overshadow the institution she represented.Such attention was far removed from the circumstances in which Mittal grew up. Born in Rewari, Haryana, she was raised in a modest household before her family moved to Delhi, which is listed as her home district in civil-service records.She studied engineering at IIT-Delhi between 2001 and 2005 and then attended IIM-Bangalore. After completing her management degree, she joined JPMorgan in London.Her husband, Gagandeep Singh Dhillon, had travelled much the same route a few years before her. He was Mittal’s senior at both IIT-Delhi and IIM-Bangalore and subsequently worked with Citigroup in London. The couple married in April 2007 and began their corporate careers in the UK.Despite well-paying jobs in international finance, they jointly decided to return to India in 2009 and prepare for the civil services. Mittal eventually joined the IAS in 2013. Dhillon entered the Indian Trade Service in 2011 and worked in areas including foreign trade and export controls.The parallel between their careers did not end there. In May 2022, Dhillon resigned from govt service and returned to financial markets. He now works as an algorithmic trader at Neuracap, according to his LinkedIn profile. Four years later, Mittal has followed him out of the civil services, although she has given no indication that she intends to return to finance.Former colleagues say Mittal’s ambition and appetite for difficult assignments were evident early in her career. Her batchmate Sunil Kumar Verma recalls that when delays arose in cadre allocation at the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, Mittal and two other officers took on the technically demanding exercise themselves and completed it for the entire batch.Some senior officers who know her describe Mittal as an “over-achiever” and believe professional stagnation may have influenced her move. Having moved rapidly from elite academic institutions and international finance to demanding district assignments, she may have found the slower phases of a bureaucratic career frustrating, they say.Her transfer from Mirzapur, extended wait for another posting, and eventual move from Deoria DM to special secretary in revenue department form part of that reading. But it’s just that: an interpretation offered by colleagues, not an explanation confirmed by Mittal.She has said her resignation was neither impulsive nor due to pressure.Her interests outside administration offer some clues, though not necessarily an answer. Mittal is the author of, “The Crafted Genius”, a book about preparation, discipline and resilience. Her social-media posts frequently discuss parenting, while her writing has examined what formal education fails to teach — emotional regulation, communication, financial management, loneliness and mental health.Mittal has indicated that writing, teaching and social service could be among the avenues she explores next.Politics is another possibility being discussed, particularly in Mirzapur, where her resignation has revived memories of her tenure. Abhinav Tripathi, pradhan of Dhawespur Kakrahi, says he would like Mittal to contest an election from the district and would contribute to her campaign if she did.The proximity of the 2027 UP assembly polls has inevitably added to that speculation. Mittal, however, has said nothing to suggest that a political debut is imminent.Her farewell note offers only one certainty: she may have surrendered the office through which she pursued her idea of public service, but she does not see herself as having surrendered the idea itself.“The position may be gone,” she wrote, “but the dream this country’s soil gave me will not leave me.”
Article Summary: Divya Mittal announced on social media that she was walking away from the civil services. The 43-year-old, 2013-batch Uttar Pradesh-cadre officer was serving as special secretary in the revenue department. Mittal has not disclosed why she quit, telling TOI that she will reveal her plans at the appropriate time.

Article Title: ‘No inconvenience to devotees’: CM Yogi Adityanath pitches grand temple complexes in Mathura-Vrindavan
Article Text:
CM Yogi Adityanath also visited the Yogmaya temple, Keshavdev temple and Bhagwat Bhavan.





MATHURA: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday said the state government plans to develop grand temple complexes in Mathura-Vrindavan on the lines of those in Ayodhya and Kashi.The statement by the chief minister came on the second day of his visit to Mathura. He arrived at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple on Friday morning on the occasion of Shri Krishna Janmashtami.The chief minister first performed ritual worship of cows in the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi complex. Following the gau pujan, Adityanath offered special prayers and sought blessings from ‘Lala’ (Lord Krishna), who is enshrined in the main sanctum sanctorum.After offering prayers in the main sanctum, Adityanath also visited the Yogmaya Temple, Keshavdev Temple and Bhagwat Bhavan, located within the complex.Speaking to the press after his visit, the CM said, "Today, you will not even be able to find invaders. They have all disappeared. A grand temple of Lord Ram has been built in Ayodhya. One of the world’s largest temples has come up in Ayodhya. Those who do not like all this are trying to defame Ayodhya.After a wait of 500 years, that work has finally been accomplished... Keeping in mind the spiritual and cultural significance of this Braj region, the Braj Teerth Vikas Parishad, along with public representatives, is working to develop it in a manner befitting its importance and to provide better facilities for devotees. Our effort is to create a similar devotee-friendly environment and infrastructure in Mathura and Vrindavan as has been developed in Ayodhya and Kashi, so that no devotee faces any inconvenience and there is no obstacle or threat to their faith."Taking a swipe at political opponents, Adityanath said his government believed in “Krishna Kanhaiya, Lord Ram, Baba Vishwanath and Maa Vindhyavasini” and respected the faith of the people.“But can those whose faith lies in Babur and Aurangzeb respect your faith?” he asked, accusing the “followers of Babur and Aurangzeb” of attempting to create divisions in society.Adityanath alleged that such forces wanted to weaken social harmony, compromise security, play with the future of young people and threaten the safety of women. He said the BJP’s “double-engine government” would not allow such designs to succeed.The chief minister also contrasted the present government’s approach with that of previous administrations, claiming that earlier governments avoided visiting such places because of “vote-bank concerns”.Referring to the changing identity of the Braj region, Adityanath said it was now being associated with religious and cultural celebrations, including Rangotsav, Braj Raj Utsav and Vaishnav Kumbh, rather than incidents of violence and disorder.Extending Janmashtami greetings to people across Uttar Pradesh, Adityanath called upon citizens to remain committed to their duties towards the country, society, Sanatan Dharma and their families.“If everyone fulfils their responsibilities honestly, it will not take long for India to become a developed nation and Uttar Pradesh a developed state,” he said.Notably, this is not the first time that the CM has spoken about developing temple complexes in Mathura on the lines of those in Ayodhya and Varanasi. He has repeatedly linked Mathura-Vrindavan’s religious development with the transformation of Ayodhya and Kashi, including in 2021-22 when he spoke about Mathura and Vrindavan after the Ram Temple and Kashi Vishwanath projects."There were numerous invasions, and many attempted to impose their own faiths upon India, yet no one could erase Sanatan Dharma. Those who had the audacity to try and obliterate Sanatan Dharma were themselves reduced to dust and faded into oblivion. However, not only in Braj Bhoomi but across all of India, the memory of Shri Krishna and Radha Rani serves as an inspiration for us today and fosters an atmosphere of enthusiasm and progress for future generations," Yogi Adityanath said.Janmashtami, also known as Krishna Janmashtami or Gokulashtami, is observed to mark the birth of Lord Krishna, regarded as the eighth avatar of Lord Vishnu.The festival is observed on the eighth day, or Ashtami, of the Krishna Paksha in the month of Bhadrapada, according to the Hindu lunisolar calendar.
Article Summary: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath visited the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple in Mathura. He also visited the Yogmaya Temple, Keshavdev Temple and Bhagwat Bhavan. He said his government believed in “Krishna Kanhaiya, Lord Ram, Baba Vishwanath and Maa Vindhyavasini’

Article Title: Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami International Airport, kills 5: Here’s the latest update shared by the company
Article Text:
Amazon cargo crash

Amazon plane crash at Miami airport

Here’s the update shared by Amazon

Updated at 3:05 p.m. PT

"We're heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today’s incident at Miami International Airport.

Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss.

The airplane, which was operated by 21 Air, was attempting to land when this incident occurred. We're working closely with local authorities and officials to learn more and will cooperate fully with any investigation." — Kelly Nantel, Amazon spokesperson

1:58 p.m. PT

"We can confirm that an Amazon Air plane operated by 21 Air experienced an incident while attempting to land at Miami International Airport today. This is a fast-moving situation and we're still gathering details. We're working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened. Right now, our absolute priority is the safety, well-being, and care of everyone involved. We're doing everything we can to support those affected.

" — Kelly Nantel, Amazon spokesperson

An Amazon cargo aircraft operated by 21 Air crashed while attempting to land at Miami International Airport on September 6, killing at least five people and injuring five others. The aircraft overran the runway and struck several vehicles before catching fire, according to local officials.vAmazon confirmed that the aircraft was an Amazon Air plane operated by 21 Air and said it was working with local authorities to understand what happened. In a latest update, the company said its priority was the safety and care of those affected by the crash.“We're heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today’s incident at Miami International Airport. Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss,” Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said in a statement shared on Amazon News website.The Boeing 767 was attempting to land when it left the usable portion of the runway and hit multiple vehicles. The crash caused a large fire, with thick black smoke visible above the airport.Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Chief Raied “Ray” Jadallah said five people were killed and another five were injured.Three of the injured were in critical condition and were taken to a trauma centre. Two others were taken to a local hospital. Several people were trapped inside vehicles struck by the aircraft and had to be removed by emergency crews.According to Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, more than 60 emergency units responded to the crash.“21 Air Flight 7598 overran the runway after landing at Miami International Airport around 2 p.m. local time on Sunday, Sept. 6. The Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft departed from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The FAA will investigate. Contact the airline for additional information,” the Federal Aviation Administration shared in a post on X.
Article Summary: The Boeing 767 was attempting to land when it left the usable portion of the runway and hit multiple vehicles. Amazon confirmed that the aircraft was an Amazon Air plane operated by 21 Air and said it was working with local authorities to understand what happened.

Article Title: Republican Mayor of American city on Lake Ontario' shore rejects the name change to 'Lake America' that Google and Apple have adopted; says: My community …
Article Text:
The renaming of ‘Lake Ontario’ and local pushback

A Bipartisan and cross-border backlash

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the economic impact of renaming Lake Ontario? It will harm local businesses It will not have much impact I'm unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The Republican mayor of Oswego, New York, Robert Corradino, has rejected the renaming of Lake Ontario to “Lake America,” a change enacted by US President Donald Trump through an executive order on August 27. While Google and Apple Maps have already adopted the new name for US users, Corradino said his community is “taking the renaming very personally” and will continue to use Lake Ontario in all signage, tourism materials, and official communications. According to a report by National Post, Corradino emphasized that Lake Ontario is central to Oswego’s identity, citing its economic importance through charter boats, cruise ships, and tourism.Corradino emphasized that Lake Ontario's name is rooted in a Huron Indigenous word meaning "lake of shining waters," predating the province of Ontario itself, which took its name from the lake in 1867. “Lake Ontario is in the DNA of Osweganians. Everything that we are emanates from the lake,” he said. The mayor also noted that Canadian tourism, vital to local businesses, has dropped substantially following the breakdown of US-Canada trade negotiations last month.Statistics Canada data shows Canadian travel to the US fell 10.6% in the first quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.Corradino reaffirmed Oswego’s stance: “Lake Ontario has carried its name for hundreds of years. It is a name rooted in history, geography, and the shared identity of the communities that surround it. The city of Oswego will continue using the name that reflects our history and honors the generations who have lived, worked, and built their lives along its shores.”Trump's order has drawn criticism well beyond Oswego. Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton responded to the renaming with a brief rebuttal on X, while Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders said the American public has no appetite for calling the lake "Lake America."North of the border, Carney noted on social media that the name Lake Ontario derives from the Wendat word "Ontari'io," meaning the lake is beautiful and big, and that it predates both Canadian Confederation and the U.S. Declaration of Independence by more than 400 years. He argued that acknowledging reality means continuing to call it Lake Ontario. Conservative Party leader Pierre Poilievre echoed the sentiment, saying the lake was never Trump's to rename on a whim.Ontario Premier Doug Ford went a step further on Saturday, unveiling a new "Lake Ontario" sign in Winona, Ontario, declaring in a video posted to X that the lake carried that name long before Trump and would continue to carry it long after he's gone.
Article Summary: The mayor of Oswego, New York, has rejected the renaming of Lake Ontario to “Lake America,” a change enacted by US President Donald Trump through an executive order on August 27. Google and Apple Maps have already adopted the new name for US users. Corradino emphasized that Lake Ontario's name is rooted in a Huron Indigenous word meaning "lake of shining waters," predating the province of Ontario.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.

Article Title: After Satya Niketan building collapse, traffic police issues advisory urges commuters to avoid key routes
Article Text:
Rescue operations underway at the Satya Niketan building collapse site





NEW DELHI: Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory on Monday after a building collapsed at Satya Niketan Market in South Campus, disrupting traffic on several key routes as rescue operations continued.In a post on X, officials said, "Following a building collapse at Satya Niketan Market, South Campus, rescue and relief operations are underway. Emergency teams are working at the spot. Traffic movement is affected on routes from Safdarjung Hospital towards Dhaula Kuan, RTR, Benito Juarez Marg AVOID THESE STRETCHES, IF POSSIBLE. Use alternate routes and follow the directions of traffic personnel. Please do not stop, park or crowd near the incident site. Keep the way clear for ambulances and rescue vehicles. Your cooperation can help save lives."The collapse has claimed six lives, while Delhi minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa said the possibility of another person remaining trapped beneath the debris could not yet be ruled out."Nothing definitive can be said yet about whether anyone else is there, as we have already accounted for students. You are aware that 12 people were rescued here, and there have been six casualties.It is suspected that there might be an unidentified labourer (inside the debris), but nothing can be confirmed until the situation is clear... The strictest possible action will definitely be taken; cases will even be registered. No one will be spared," Sirsa told reporters.The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is continuing its search and rescue operation. Sirsa said the condition and age of a neighbouring structure had made the operation more difficult."The NDRF team is continuously engaged in the operation. You can see that this situation involves a high degree of sensitivity because the building visible in the background is also 40–50 years old. It poses a major challenge for the NDRF to ensure no damage occurs to the adjacent building while clearing the debris from below and checking for any further casualties. However, the NDRF is a highly capable force; I have gathered information and spoken with the NDRF chief. The adjacent building will definitely be demolished—it has already been evacuated and is slated for demolition. But the challenge right now is that the structure is currently unstable; we do not yet know the condition beneath the accumulated debris, so it cannot be demolished immediately... The information received so far indicates that while this building was 40–50 years old, attempts were made to carry out work in its basement, which triggered this accident. The Chief Minister stated yesterday itself that strict action would be taken regarding the issues raised," he told reporters.The death toll rose to six after another body was recovered during rescue operations late on Sunday night. Twelve people have been rescued so far, with the NDRF, Delhi Fire Service, Delhi Police and other agencies continuing to clear the debris and search for anyone who may still be trapped.The collapse has also raised questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest accommodation and the enforcement of construction and fire safety rules in densely populated parts of Delhi.
Article Summary: Delhi Traffic Police issue advisory after building collapses at Satya Niketan Market. Traffic movement affected on routes from Safdarjung Hospital towards Dhaula Kuan, RTR, Benito Juarez Marg. Death toll rises to six after another body was recovered during rescue operations late on Sunday night.
